cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The prior B0 combined semantic contracts, evidence production, process execution, and native containment, which exposed caller-minting and incomplete binding risks while expanding to 5,897 lines.
impact: B0 is reduced to generic authority contracts, canonical attestations, and fail-closed verification; native containment and statistical evidence production now have separate producers and acceptance gates.
lesson: Keep the trust core smaller than the execution system and bind domain contracts by digest instead of placing model or data semantics in the root security protocol.

cause: The four allowed documents were checked after the final edits with the naming gate, diff check, stale-reference scan, and formal FMS verification.
impact: Twenty-two naming tests passed, git diff check was clean, stale B0-R2 implementation references were absent from the four live documents, and the formal line verified.
lesson: A trust-boundary redesign is accepted only when the semantic specification, implementation lane, execution DAG, and formal scope all describe the same producer and verifier responsibilities.

cause: The approved B0 redesign is reflected in the four existing authoritative documents without adding retained specifications, objectives, plans, reviews, or handoffs.
impact: The next implementation line can build the small B0 authority/verifier core, while B1 native containment and CF3 statistical evidence remain separately gated.
lesson: Preserve one live document map and revise it in place when a security boundary changes.
